newsitem.title: CHINA: China's A, B shares up on renewed confidence.
newsitem.headline: China's A, B shares up on renewed confidence.

text.p: China's A and B share indices ended up across the board on Monday on renewed confidence after an official newspaper said excessive speculation on the stock markets had been effectively checked, traders said.
Shenzhen stocks rose sharply with A share index up 24.1 points or 7.25 percent to 356.4 points and the B share index up 12.85 points or 9.03 percent to 155.19 points.
On the Shanghai market, the A share index gained 12.565 points or 1.31 percent to 973.467 points and the B index edged up 0.426 points or 0.64 percent to 67.061 points.
A commentary by the People's Daily, the mouthpiece of the Communist Party, said last Friday that after a recent crackdown on the stock markets, excessive speculation had been checked.

"The day's surges were due to that commentary, which was interpreted by investors as a sign that Beijing does not intend to take new measures to further cool down stock trading," a Shenzhen-based analyst said.
Brokers said that buying was now expected to generally shift to shares in firms likely to report strong results for 1996.

On the Shenzhen market, Shenzhen Zhonghao B share closed at its limit-up of HK$4.24 on volume of 465,521 shares and Changan Automobile traded the most on volume of 5.11 million shares and rose HK$0.44 to HK$4.85 on demand by domestic institutions, brokers said.
Automobile parts maker Zhuzhou Torch A share rose 0.43 yuan to its daily limit-up of 4.68 yuan.
On Shanghai's B share market, real estate developer Lujiazui traded the most, rising $0.014 or 1.07 percent to $1.316 on volume of 2.5 million shares.
Lujiazui fell sharply last week due to the dilution of the value of its existing shares by a three-for-10 rights issue earlier this month, brokers said.
Gold producer Luyin Group was the star on Shanghai A share market, soaring 1.62 yuan or 10.00 percent to 17.80 yuan, on volume of 3.4 million shares.
